intro: Cabinetmakers measure precisely, check quality and run shop machines, skills that metal fabrication and construction trades reward. The closest of the 25 careers below is Layout Workers, Metal and Plastic, with an 86% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $63,870, which is 37% more than the $46,680 cabinetmakers earn.
why_it_works: Building cabinets means reading drawings, setting up saws and routers and fitting parts that must line up exactly. O*NET rates operations monitoring at 3.38 out of 5 for this job and quality control analysis at 3.25. Layout, metal fabrication and boilermaking use the same precision with different materials. Almost every match needs no extra schooling. The gaps are repairing machines and teaching others.
tips: Boilermakers earn $76,410, which is 64% more, and are an 81% match through apprenticeships.
Terrazzo Workers and Finishers earn $76,170, or 63% more, and value fine finishing work.
Learn to set up CNC routers; automated shops pay more than manual ones.

faq.q: What jobs can former cabinetmakers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are metal and plastic layout workers (86%), Structural Metal Fabricators and Fitters (84%) and Boilermakers (81%), based on O*NET 31.0. Structural fabricators earn $51,330, which is 10% more than the $46,680 median for cabinetmakers and bench carpenters.

faq.q: Which careers for cabinetmakers pay more?
faq.a: 17 of the 25 matches pay more. Boilermakers earn $76,410 (64% more), Terrazzo Workers and Finishers $76,170 (63% more) and Pile Driver Operators $73,300 (57% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Most train through apprenticeships or on the job.

faq.q: Do cabinetmakers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than cabinetmakers already have, including 9 of the top 10. In the closest match, 60% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, so trade certificates count most.

The skills that most often need work are operation and control, repairing, instructing and operations monitoring. Time management already rates 3 out of 5 for cabinetmakers in O*NET, so running and maintaining industrial equipment is the main step toward better-paid trades.
